I have the same issue on Fedora 43 Silverblue, native, and OpenCode 1.4.10

## 📝 Comment 1: Explore findings

**Exploración completada.**

Archivos analizados:
- `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/component/prompt/index.tsx` - keyboard handler
- `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/component/textarea-keybindings.ts` - keybindings

**Root cause:** Líneas 931-957 en index.tsx bloqueaban TODOS los keys con meta/ctrl si el clipboard tenía contenido, incluyendo Cmd+V.

## 📝 Comment 2: Spec

**Requisitos:**
1. Cmd+V siempre debe hacer paste (no exit)
2. Cmd+C debe seguir funcionando (copy)
3. Exit solo con Escape cuando input vacío
4. No romper otras funciones de teclado

**Escenarios:**
- [ ] Cmd+V con texto en clipboard → pega texto
- [ ] Cmd+V con imagen en clipboard → pega imagen
- [ ] Cmd+V sin contenido → comportamiento normal
- [ ] Escape con input vacío → exit
- [ ] Escape con texto → NO exit

## 📝 Comment 4: Tasks checklist

- [x] 1. Analizar código existente
- [x] 2. Identificar root cause
- [x] 3. Implementar fix en index.tsx
- [ ] 4. Testear Cmd+V para paste
- [ ] 5. Testear Escape para exit
- [ ] 6. Verificar que Cmd+C funciona

## 📝 Comment 5: Apply (implementación)

**Fix aplicado en:**
- Rama: `fix/cmd-v-paste`
- Archivo: `packages/opencode/src/cli/cmd/tui/component/prompt/index.tsx`
- Líneas: 931-953

**Cambios:**
- Simplificada la lógica de detección
- Cmd+V ahora siempre hace paste
- Otros meta/ctrl combos bloqueados para prevenir exit accidental

## 📝 Comment 6: Verify

**Resultado inicial:** El fix funciona en testing inicial.

**Pendiente testing completo:**
- [ ] Cmd+V con diferentes tipos de contenido
- [ ] Cmd+C copy sigue funcionando
- [ ] Escape exit funciona

I encountered the same issue. here is my workaround.

Workaround that fixed it for me without any code change — just config.
Drop this into `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (global) to bind `Ctrl+X V` as a fallback for `Ctrl+V`:
```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "keybinds": {
    "input_paste": "ctrl+v,<leader>v"
  }
}
```

Default leader is Ctrl+X, so Ctrl+X then V triggers the same paste path. Because V arrives as a regular keypress after Ctrl+X, the terminal has no reason to intercept it, which bypasses whatever swallows Ctrl+V.

Environment where this was confirmed working:
- opencode: 1.4.11
- Windows Terminal on Windows 11: 1.24.10921.0
- WSL: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS on WSL2 (kernel 6.6.87.2)

In my case, the agent had just run git merge origin/dev 2>&1 (which reported 4 conflicts), then ran grep -n to locate conflict markers in one of the files. After that, the TUI showed ~ Writing command... and got stuck there.

- ESC did not work — the UI was visually responsive (I could scroll, etc.) but pressing ESC had no effect on stopping the agent
- Had to force-kill the process to regain control
- After restarting and telling the agent to continue, it resumed conflict resolution normally

This matches the description: the abort signal is no longer plumbed through to shell execution, so ESC cannot interrupt.
